zones.label: Column 1
zones.note: Lexical aid consulted after independent scan reading: Entry Words Data of Nippojisho, NINJAL, Hideyuki Ohshima and Taichi Aida, version 202510, CC BY 4.0 ([source](https://www2.ninjal.ac.jp/textdb_dataset/en/nipp/index.html); [license](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/)). The diplomatic readings and English notes in this return are scan-based review work, not a reproduction of that index.

lines.note: This carries over an example from the preceding page: the Portuguese describes remaining humbly. The initial fragment is preserved without reconstructing the missing beginning; the final S. is a roman usage label. Typeface update: S. is provisionally italicized under the bulk convention.
Ken is equated with tsurugi, a sword. The example begins ken wo nuki-, and the printed hyphen connects it to the following physical row.
Completes nuki kutsuroguru, loosening or partly drawing the sword. The Portuguese specifies drawing half the sword; historical mea is retained rather than modernized to meia.
Ken wo tai suru means carrying or wearing a sword, matching trazer espada. The printed separation tai ſuru is retained.
Ken wo nuki hanasu means drawing the sword completely. The scan supports the object-particle sequence Qenuo rather than OCR Qenno; the Portuguese todo is divided here.
Do completes de todo. The next sword example, sashi kazasu, is explained as placing or holding the sword upright; espada continues on the next row.
The sword is held upright before the face. Ken wo furu introduces swinging it; retain the source's roſto spelling pending the separate st-ligature audit.
The Latin alternative marker l introduces tsukau, another expression for wielding the sword. Iugar da espada gives the fencing sense, not ordinary playing with an object.
Kenage denotes valour or strength here. The historical meaning is established by the paired Portuguese nouns, rather than the narrower associations of the modern Japanese adjective.
Kenage date is a display of bravery. The repeated expression starts at the right edge and continues after the visible Qe- division.
Completes kenage date wo suru, making a show of bravery. The Portuguese offers two equivalent constructions for showing or giving signs of it.
De valente completes the preceding Portuguese expression: giving signs of being brave. This short continuation belongs to the same example.
Kenage na is glossed both as brave and as sound or healthy. Preserve the printed adjective and the tilde on the final vowel of ſaõ.
Kenage ni is the corresponding adverb. Adu. belongs to the italic grammatical apparatus; the second Portuguese explanation continues below.
The adverb can describe health and good condition. Vt introduces kenage ni gozaru, rather than another headword.
Gozaru completes the example, rendered as being healthy and well disposed. The historical Portuguese deſpoſto is retained rather than regularized to disposto.
Kenai is explained by ie no uchi, the household. The Portuguese describes a family or the people of a house, with the final noun continued below.
Casa completes the household gloss. Kenai no mono is given as an equivalent expression for members of that household.

runs.text: Couſa de que ſe tem enueja em boa

lines.note: Kenarige concerns something regarded with envy or admiration. The qualification em boa parte continues below and makes this a favourable rather than malicious sense.

runs.text: parte, ou que ſe deſeja imitar, ou auer. Vt,

lines.note: The desirable thing is something one wishes to imitate or possess. This completes the favourable sense of envy and introduces the following example.
Kenarige ni miyuru is rendered as seeming to desire something. The Portuguese subject remains implicit; its alternative explanation continues on the next row.

runs.text: ou tem enueja in bonam partem.

lines.note: The alternative is having envy in a good sense. The Latin phrase in bonam partem is printed within the italic explanatory passage, not as Japanese text.
Kenarii and kenarii koto are referred back to the same meaning. The lowercase alternative after l is preserved, as is the final ij spelling.
Kenba is explained as dog and horse, inu and uma. The visible descending stroke identifies the initial as Q, correcting OCR Cenba.

runs.text: Doença dos ombros. No Ximo: ẽ

lines.note: Kenbeki is a shoulder ailment. Ximo is an embedded regional name; the visibly slanted lowercase letters support retaining the italic treatment of the explanatory passage, rather than making the term uniformly roman. The following mark is read as a colon and the nasalized ẽ is retained; the compressed regional wording is not silently rewritten.
The regional explanation supplies heki as another name. Feqi is a Japanese word embedded in the Portuguese naming construction, not a new independent headword.

runs.text: Certos bolos de farinha de trigo, ou

lines.note: Kenbin names cakes made from wheat flour. The Portuguese continues with a comparison to another kind of cake rather than identifying a second Japanese term.

runs.text: filhòs aſados de maneira queſe dobrão como o-

lines.note: The cakes are described as baked and folded like thick wafers. The printed single s in aſados and the contiguous queſe are retained; o- begins obreas on the next row.
Breas completes obreas, wafers, qualified as thick. This short line finishes the description of kenbin.
Kenbou is glossed as justice. The visible caron is preserved; the provisional st classification in Iustiça is left for the dedicated typography audit.
Kenbou na describes something upright or just. This is the adjectival member of the family continuing in the two indented rows below.
Kenbou ni supplies the adverbial form, with the italic abbreviation Adu. Its indentation associates it with the preceding justice entry.
Kenbousa gives the corresponding quality noun. The row has no separate Portuguese gloss; its interpretation follows the adjacent adjective and adverb.

runs.text: O ver algũ a couſa, ou vista de al-

lines.note: Kenbutsu concerns seeing or viewing something. The printed space within algũ a is retained as source evidence, and the second alguma is divided at the line end.

runs.text: gũa couſa por nouidade, ou recreação. Vt,

lines.note: The viewing is undertaken for novelty or recreation. Vt introduces the example of an unprecedented sight on the following row.

Zendai mimon no kenbutsu nari describes an unprecedented spectacle. The scan joins qenbut, correcting the OCR's internal space; initial Ien has the consonantal value explained in the supplied historical notes.

runs.text: ſta que tègora ſe não vio, nem ouuio tal.

lines.note: Completes vista: a sight whose like has not previously been seen or heard of. Tègora is retained as the printed historical expression for 'until now'.

runs.text: Os que vem de nouo, ou por re-

lines.note: Kenbutsusha denotes spectators. Here vem belongs to ver, seeing, in the description of people viewing something for novelty or recreation; it is not modernized with an accent.
Completes recreação and the spectators' act of viewing something. The nasal mark in algũa remains on u as printed.
Kenka is glossed as a chief governor. The damaged initial retains the visible Q outline; this is a separate office-title entry, not the later word for a quarrel.
Kenkaku is a man carrying a sword. Mi- begins michi in the following example; it is a genuine divided Japanese word.

runs.text: chini qencacuni vǒte, ſubecaracu maſu be

lines.note: The example describes meeting a swordsman on the road and what one should then do. The scan reads maſu be, although the Portuguese suggests readying or sharpening one's sword; no inferred Japanese replacement is supplied.

runs.text: Se encontrares com homem que traz eſ-

lines.note: Xi completes bexi, the modal beshi. The Portuguese begins the condition 'if you meet a man carrying a sword', with espada divided across rows.

runs.text: pida, tu tambem concerta, & afia tu eſpa-

lines.note: The gloss advises likewise putting one's sword in order and sharpening it. The first vowel in the damaged pida fragment remains uncertain; the retained surface reading is contextually espada, not a different lexical item.
Completes espada and adds the explanatory imperative Preparate, 'prepare yourself'. The physical division and the source's unaccented joined form are preserved.
Kenchi is the 'pond' of an inkstone, suzuri no ike. The Portuguese identifies the hollow in the stone inkwell; q̃ is an abbreviation, not an expanded que.

runs.text: de pedra da China com agoa pera moer a tin-

lines.note: The hollow contains water for grinding ink on a Chinese stone inkstone. Historical agoa and pera are retained, and tinta continues below.
Ta completes tinta. The final upright S. labels this written usage and is not part of the italic Portuguese gloss. Typeface update: S. is provisionally italicized under the bulk convention.
This kenchi is wise understanding, explained by kashikoi chie. The Portuguese prudencia is divided without a securely readable hyphen, so none is supplied.
Cia completes prudencia. Kenchi naru hito supplies a person characterized by this wisdom; the Portuguese noun phrase continues below.
Completes the description as a person of sound knowledge and prudence. This is the gloss of the preceding Japanese example, not a further headword.
A distinct kenchi denotes land measurement or surveying. The example begins kenchi wo and is completed by suru on the next row.
Suru completes 'carry out a land survey'. It is a genuine short Japanese continuation, with no independent Portuguese gloss.
Kencho denotes something evident or revealed. The unmarked final o is preserved; no modern long-vowel spelling is imposed.
Kencho nari means that something is evident. The final S. is printed upright as the written-usage label. Typeface update: S. is provisionally italicized under the bulk convention.
Kencho na hito describes an open or straightforward person. The repeated Qenchona, confirmed by the scan and entry heading, corrects OCR Qeachona.
Describing the person as open and clear completes the example. The Portuguese qualities explain the figurative human application of the preceding adjective.
This separately accented kenchouna describes someone easily frightened. Its circumflex distinguishes it from the preceding unaccented forms; the visibly abbreviated facelmẽte is retained.
Kenkou denotes strength or hardness. The initial is a roman Q, not an italic O, and the caron contrasts with the circumflex in the next entry.
This kenkou combines sword and helmet, tsurugi and kabuto. The scan's line-end mark divides capacete; the OCR period is corrected to a hyphen.
Pacete completes capacete, helmet. The final S. is a roman written-usage label for the sword-and-helmet entry. Typeface update: S. is provisionally italicized under the bulk convention.

Kenkon is equated with tenchi, heaven and earth. The synonym after i is not an embedded word in a Portuguese sentence; the final S. remains upright. Typeface update: S. is provisionally italicized under the bulk convention.
Kenkun means a wise lord, kashikoi kimi. The Q tail corrects OCR Gencun, and the abbreviated prudẽte preserves the printed nasal mark.

runs.text: Certa estante que ſerue de pòr o liuro.

lines.note: Kendai denotes a stand on which a book is placed. The initial is a roman Q rather than the OCR's italic O; the grave in pòr is preserved.
Kendan is the office or function of governing and judging. The Portuguese describes an administrative role rather than a physical object.
Kendan suru means carrying out that office. The visible paragraph mark omitted by OCR is restored; the comparison with a presiding official continues below.
Completes the explanation as acting in the capacity of a president or presiding official. The scan supplies both the space and the missing i in de preſidente.
Kendannin names the person holding the office: a president, governor, or judge. The final alternative continues on the next physical row.
The third equivalent is a judge of some locality. Dalgum remains joined as printed and completes the preceding entry.
Kendon is cruelty or inhumanity. The small but visible e restores Crueza from OCR Cruza without modernizing the historical noun.
Kendon houitsu is assigned the same sense. The initial Q, damaged but matching its neighbours, corrects OCR Dendon; the checked final t is preserved.
Kendon na is the adjectival form, describing something cruel and inhuman. Its doubled n corresponds to the source's stem-plus-na spelling.
Kendon ni is the adverbial form. The Portuguese uses the shared -mente construction, with deshumanamente divided after deſhumana and no added hyphen.
Mente completes the adverbial gloss 'cruelly and inhumanly'. Its shortness does not make it furniture or a separate entry.

runs.text: O vir, ou o correr ao penſamento. S.

lines.note: Kenen is described as something coming or running into one's thoughts. The printed S. is the upright label for written usage. Typeface update: S. is provisionally italicized under the bulk convention.
Kengaku is a great difference or separation, explained by haruka ni hedataru. The following clouds-and-mud comparison illustrates the scale of that difference.
Undei no kengaku nari describes a difference like that between clouds and mud. The scan contains a paragraph mark before the example, restored here from the OCR omission.

runs.text: ça como de nuuẽs, & lama. S.

lines.note: Completes differença and explicitly compares clouds with mud. The nasal abbreviation in nuuẽs and the roman S. are preserved. Typeface update: S. is provisionally italicized under the bulk convention.
A separate kengaku is explained by kanete manabu, studying beforehand. The Portuguese offers both the noun study and a completed prior act.
Ter estudado dantes means having studied previously. The final S. belongs to the usage apparatus and is upright. Typeface update: S. is provisionally italicized under the bulk convention.
Kenjo is a wise woman, kashikoki onna. The historical vonna spelling and the visible division of abbreviated prudẽte remain unchanged.

runs.text: te, & acautelada, & q̃ não ouue quaes quer

lines.note: The woman is prudent and cautious and does not listen to harmful persuasion. Quaes quer remains two printed words; q̃ is not expanded.
Bad persuasions or counsels complete the preceding relative clause. This qualification belongs to the definition of the prudent woman.

runs.text: Qengo. Cataxi, cataxi. i, Tçuyoi coto.

lines.note: Kengo denotes firmness or strength. The repeated kataxi is printed intentionally as the Japanese explanatory sequence; Cou begins couſa below without a supplied hyphen.
Completes couſa forte, a strong thing. This short continuation belongs to kengo and does not introduce an additional entry.
Kengo na is illustrated with a strong or brave person. The scan supports the anomalous Cauſa rather than expected Couſa, so that spelling is preserved and flagged rather than emended.
To completes hito in kengo na hito. The Portuguese explicitly gives a strong and valiant man.
Kengo ni is the adverb, strongly or firmly. Qen- begins kenzoku in the following example about the household's condition.
Kenzoku izure mo kengo ni gozaru says that all the household are well. The printed doubled zz in izzuremo is retained, and gente is divided at the line end.

runs.text: te de caſa toda està bem, & em paz, ou bem

lines.note: Completes gente and explains that everyone in the house is well and at peace. The alternative bem deſpoſta continues on the next row.
Deſpoſta completes the statement that the household is in good condition. The feminine form agrees with gente, not with a new Japanese noun.
Kengoshin is fortitude or a strong heart. The compound's mental quality is explicit in the second Portuguese equivalent.
Kengu contrasts a wise person with a foolish one. The scan ends mono with a period, correcting the OCR hyphen; the whole Japanese explanation remains roman.

runs.text: Homem prudente, & homem paruo, ou ig-

lines.note: The Portuguese likewise contrasts a prudent man with a foolish or ignorant man. Ignorante is visibly divided after ig-.
Norante completes ignorante and the wise-versus-foolish entry. The signature and catchword below it are separate page furniture, not additional body text.
